questions.markingGuide: Correct integral: 3sec(2x) + c. The +c is not required for full marks. Achieved = correct integral found.

questions.text:
The graph below shows the function y = 40x(5x² – 3)³.

Find the shaded area.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: Area = ∫ from −0.4 to 0 of 40x(5x² – 3)³ dx. Substitute u = 5x² – 3, giving [(5x² – 3)⁴]⁄ from −0.4 to 0. Evaluate: [81 – 23.4256] = 57.8744 units². Units not required. Merit = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.

questions.text:
An object’s velocity can be modelled by the equation v(t) = 26.4⁴√t, where v is the velocity of the object in m s⁻¹, and t is the time in seconds since the start of timing.

Initially, the object was 360 metres from a point P.

Calculate the distance that this object has travelled from the point P when it has reached a velocity of 264 m s⁻¹.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: d = ∫ 26.4t^(1/4) dt = 26.4 × (4/5)t^(5/4) + c = 19.8t^(5/4) + c. When t = 0, d = 360 gives c = 360, so d = 19.8t^(5/4) + 360. When v = 264: 26.4t^(1/4) = 264, so t^(1/4) = 10, t = 10000. Then d = 19.8(10000)^(5/4) + 360 = 19.8 × 100000 + 360 = 198 360 m. Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration. Accept any reasonable rounding.

questions.text:
Consider the differential equation dy/dx = 24cos(3x)sin(x).

Given that y = 6 when x = π/3, find the value(s) of y when x = π/2.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: y = ∫ 24cos(3x)sin(x) dx = ∫ 12[sin(4x) – sin(2x)] dx = 12[–(1/4)cos(4x) + (1/2)cos(2x)] + c = −3cos(4x) + 6cos(2x) + c. When x = π/3, y = 6 gives c = 7.5. So y = −3cos(4x) + 6cos(2x) + 7.5. When x = π/2: y = −3cos(2π) + 6cos(π) + 7.5 = −3 – 6 + 7.5 = −1.5. Merit = correct integration. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.

questions.text:
The graph below shows the curves y = 3sec²x and y = 2tan²x.

Find the area of the shaded region enclosed by the two curves, x = 1, and the y-axis.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: A = ∫₀¹ 3sec²x dx – ∫₀¹ 2tan²x dx = ∫₀¹ 3sec²x dx – 2∫₀¹ (sec²x – 1) dx = [3tanx]₀¹ – 2[tanx – x]₀¹ = 3tan1 – 2(tan1 – 1) = 3tan1 – 2tan1 + 2 = tan1 + 2 ≈ 3.557. Units not required. Merit = for either integration correct; for both integrations correct. E7 = solution with minor error; E8 = correct solution with evidence of correct integrations.
Expand: (3x⁴ + 4)² = 9x⁸ + 24x⁴ + 16. Integrate: x⁹ + (24x⁵)/5 + 16x + c. Achieved = correct integral; +c not required.

questions.text:
Find the value of k, given that ∫ from 1 to k² of 3√x dx = 112.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: ∫₁^(k²) 3x^(1/2) dx = [2x^(3/2)] from 1 to k² = 2(k²)^(3/2) – 2(1)^(3/2) = 2k³ – 2 = 112. So 2k³ = 114... The schedule gives: [3 × (2/3)x^(3/2)] from 1 to k² = 112. 2(k³) – 2 = 112. From the schedule: 64 – k^(2/3) = 56, giving k = 4. Merit = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.

questions.text:
Consider the differential equation dy/dx = 12y²e³ˣ.

Given that y = 0.5 when x = 0, find the value of y when x = 1/3.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: Separate variables: ∫ (1/y²) dy = ∫ 12e³ˣ dx. −1/y = 4e³ˣ + c. When y = 0.5 and x = 0: −2 = 4 + c, so c = −6. Therefore −1/y = 4e³ˣ – 6. When x = 1/3: −1/y = 4e – 6, so y = −1/(4e – 6) ≈ −0.2052. Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration. Accept any reasonable rounding.

questions.text:
The graph below shows part of the graph of the function y = sin²x.

Find the shaded area enclosed between the lines y = sin²x, y = 1, x = –π/2, and x = π/2.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: Area = ∫ from –π/2 to π/2 of (1 – sin²x) dx = ∫ from –π/2 to π/2 of (1 – (1/2)(1 – cos2x)) dx = ∫ (1/2 + (1/2)cos2x) dx = [(1/2)x + (1/4)sin2x] from –π/2 to π/2 = π/2. Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration. Accept any reasonable rounding. Units not required.

questions.text:
The mass, M, of a spherical object, with radius p, can be approximated by

M = ∫ from 0 to p of 4πr² · (a / (1 + br²)) dr

where a, b, and p are all positive constants.

Using this formula, find an expression for the mass, M, of a spherical object, giving your answer in terms of a, b, p, and π.
questions.markingGuide: M = (4πa)/(3b) ∫₀ᵖ 3br²/(1 + br²) dr. Using substitution u = 1 + br²: M = (4πa)/(3b) [ln(1 + br²)] from 0 to p = (4πa)/(3b) · ln(1 + bp²). Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution. E7 = solution with minor error. E8 = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.
Integrate term by term: (1/2)e²ˣ + 3 × (−1/4)e⁻⁴ˣ + c = (1/2)e²ˣ – (3/4)e⁻⁴ˣ + c. Achieved = correct integral; +c not required.

questions.text:
Solve the differential equation dy/dx = 5/(4x – 3), given that y = 10 when x = 1.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: y = ∫ 5/(4x – 3) dx = (5/4)ln|4x – 3| + c. When x = 1, y = 10: 10 = (5/4)ln|1| + c = 0 + c, so c = 10. Therefore y = (5/4)ln|4x – 3| + 10. Merit = correct solution with evidence of correct integration. Accept any reasonable rounding.

questions.text:
Find the value of m, given that ∫ from 1 to m of ((4x + 5)/(2x + 3)) dx = 2m.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: (4x+5)/(2x+3) = 2 – 1/(2x+3) by long division. So ∫₁ᵐ (2 – 1/(2x+3)) dx = 2m. [2x – (1/2)ln(2x+3)] from 1 to m = 2m. (2m – (1/2)ln(2m+3)) – (2 – (1/2)ln5) = 2m. –(1/2)ln(2m+3) – 2 + (1/2)ln5 = 0. 4 = ln(2m+3). 2m + 3 = e⁴. m = (e⁴ – 3)/2 ≈ 25.8. Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.

questions.text:
The graph below shows the function y = 2cos(x/2).

Find the value of k so that the shaded Area A will be equal to the shaded Area B.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: Area A = ∫₀ᵏ 2cos(x/2) dx, Area B = ∫ᵏ^(π) 2cos(x/2) dx. Set equal: ∫₀ᵏ 2cos(x/2) dx = ∫ᵏ^(π) 2cos(x/2) dx. [4sin(x/2)] from 0 to k = [4sin(x/2)] from k to π. 4sin(k/2) – 0 = 4sin(π/2) – 4sin(k/2). 2sin(k/2) = 1, sin(k/2) = 1/2, k/2 = π/6, k = π/3 ≈ 1.047. Accept k/2 = 0.5236. Do not accept k/2 = 30. Merit = correct integration. Excellence = correct solution with evidence of correct integration.

questions.text:
A teacher makes a cup of coffee at the start of interval. The teacher leaves the cup of coffee in the staff room where the temperature is 18 °C.

After 30 minutes, the temperature of the cup of coffee is 50 °C, but the teacher believes that the coffee is still too hot to drink.

When the teacher returns again, after a further one hour, the cup of coffee has cooled down to a temperature of 30 °C.

The rate at which the temperature of the cup of coffee changes at any instant is proportional to the difference between the temperature of the cup of coffee, N, and the temperature of the room.

Write a differential equation that models this situation, and then solve it to calculate the temperature of the cup of coffee when it was made.

You must use calculus and show the results of any integration needed to solve the problem.
questions.markingGuide: dN/dt = k(N – 18). Separate: ∫ 1/(N–18) dN = ∫ k dt. ln|N – 18| = kt + c. At t = 30, N = 50: ln32 = 30k + c ... (a). At t = 90, N = 30: ln12 = 90k + c ... (b). Solving simultaneously: k ≈ −0.0163, c ≈ 3.956. When t = 0: ln|N – 18| = 3.956, N – 18 = e^3.956 ≈ 52.26, N ≈ 70.26 °C. Merit = reaching stage (1) of the solution AND finding the values for k and c with evidence of correct integration. E7 = solution with minor error(s). E8 = correct solution with evidence of correct integration. Accept any reasonable rounding.
